## Context / Problem
The edit-then-re-review loop is common and hazardous as two shell commands, and claim's recovery text (src/rebar/_commands/gates.py:213-215) tells the user to run review-plan then claim by hand. Operator approved both flags. OSS precedent favors embedding prerequisite verification in the consuming verb (cargo publish verifies by default; terraform apply consumes a staleness-checked plan artifact) over new fused commands.

## Approach
(1) `rebar edit <id> ... --review`: edit_cli's hand-rolled parser (src/rebar/_commands/composer.py:528-561) treats every --name as requiring a value, so `--review` is handled as an explicit valueless flag checked BEFORE the field loop (popped from argv, bypassing the --key=value pathway); after edit_core commits the EDIT event, invoke rebar.llm.review_plan(ticket_id, sign=True) and map the returned verdict dict to the process exit status with the disposition mapping (0 PASS / 1 BLOCK / 2 INDETERMINATE / 11 retryable per ADR 0040). _disposition_exit_code stays in src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py; the flag handlers use a lazy in-function import (`from rebar._cli._llm_commands import _disposition_exit_code`) — the established pattern for a _commands module reaching a _cli helper, per the existing lazy `from rebar._cli import _help` inside reopen_cli at src/rebar/_commands/transition.py:562. No file moves. (2) `rebar claim <id> --review`: implemented as a new keyword parameter review: bool = False on claim_compute, threaded from claim_cli's parser; the logic sits inside claim_compute at the claim.py:133 seam: when --review is set and the gate applies, call llm.claim_gate_check(ticket_id); if it reports not-ok, run review_plan(sign=True). The review verdict then determines control flow exactly: on PASS, proceed into the normal plan_review_precheck path and claim (precheck re-checks and fails closed with the standard message if the attestation is somehow still stale); on BLOCK, INDETERMINATE, or a retryable degrade, the claim is NOT attempted — the command prints the review's finding summary and exits with the disposition mapping applied to the review result (1 / 2 / 11 respectively), leaving the ticket open for revision. When the gate is disabled or the ticket type is exempt (plan_review_precheck would return None), --review prints a one-line notice "plan-review gate not enabled for this ticket; --review skipped" and the claim proceeds — never a silent no-op. The flag is NOT propagated through the parent-first cascade. (3) Help and docs: the real help sources are src/rebar/_cli/help/edit.txt and src/rebar/_cli/help/claim.txt; docs/cli-reference.md is generated by scripts/gen_cli_reference.py and is regenerated, not hand-edited. Both help texts state the flags are not atomic against concurrent store reconvergence and point at `review-plan --status`. Lock discipline: neither flag holds the store flock across the review — the edit/claim appends its own event under the normal short-lived lock, releases it, and only then invokes review_plan, which itself takes the lock only for the brief under-lock generation re-check at signing; the multi-minute LLM passes run with no lock held. Both flags are CLI-only (the MCP surface keeps its REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM fence). Alternative rejected: new fused verbs — no OSS precedent, larger surface.

## Scope
src/rebar/_commands/composer.py, src/rebar/_commands/claim.py, src/rebar/_cli/help/edit.txt, src/rebar/_cli/help/claim.txt, docs/cli-reference.md (regenerated via scripts/gen_cli_reference.py), docs/exit-codes.md (document the --review exit codes for edit and claim — the new codes apply only when the flag is passed; the flagless contracts are unchanged), tests/unit/test_review_flags.py (new).

## Testing
Unit with a stubbed review_plan returning verdict dicts: bare `--review` parses without consuming a following token (an edit with `--review --priority 1` keeps both); edit --review runs review after the EDIT commit and maps PASS/BLOCK/INDETERMINATE stubs to exits 0/1/2; a BLOCK leaves the edit committed; claim --review claims on a PASS stub, and on BLOCK, INDETERMINATE, and retryable-degrade stubs never calls the claim core and exits 1, 2, and 11 respectively; it prints the gate-disabled notice for a bug-type ticket and claims anyway; it fails closed when the post-review recheck still reports stale; the parent cascade never receives the flag; a review stub that itself acquires the store flock succeeds under both flags.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Bare --review parses as a valueless flag without swallowing the next token (checked: parser unit test).
- [ ] edit --review runs the review strictly after the EDIT commit and exits with _disposition_exit_code(result, indeterminate_code=2) (checked: unit test recording call order and exit codes for PASS/BLOCK/INDETERMINATE stubs).
- [ ] claim --review claims only on PASS; on BLOCK/INDETERMINATE/retryable-degrade it never invokes the claim core and exits 1/2/11 with the review summary printed (checked: unit tests with stubbed verdicts, including a retryable stub, asserting the claim core is not called).
- [ ] Both flag handlers obtain _disposition_exit_code via the lazy in-function import and the review-plan CLI's own exit-code behavior is unchanged (checked: unit test asserting the mapped exit codes; existing review-plan CLI exit-code tests pass).
- [ ] claim --review reviews only when claim_gate_check reports not-ok, prints the skip notice when the gate does not apply, and never propagates through the parent cascade (checked: unit tests).
- [ ] Help sources document non-atomicity and reference review-plan --status, and docs/cli-reference.md is regenerated (checked: help-text assertions; regenerated file committed).
- [ ] docs/exit-codes.md documents the --review exit codes for edit and claim and states the flagless contracts are unchanged (checked: doc text assertion; existing exit-code conformance tests pass).
- [ ] The store lock is not held while the review runs: a review stub that acquires the store flock succeeds under both flags (checked: unit test).
